questions.q: A director announces that a classic play is 'really about the collapse of Western civilization' and builds every design choice around that reading. What would Sontag object to?
choices: The production lacks a clear premise to prove
The director has replaced the play with an interpretation of it
The play's inciting incident comes too late
The audience will identify too closely with the hero
questions.explain: Sontag's example was Kazan's notes on Streetcar: staging the interpretation rather than the play.

questions.q: What does Sontag propose in place of interpretation?
choices: A criticism attentive to form and experience: an erotics of art
A search for the work's controlling idea
A list of the work's functions in order
A reading based on the author's biography
questions.explain: She wants criticism to show how a work is what it is, not what it means.

questions.q: A screenwriting teacher tells students to write their theme as a single sentence before drafting. Which tension does Sontag's essay highlight?
choices: Between plot and character, as Aristotle ranked them
Between information and story
Between theme-first advice and a work's sensuous experience, which a theme statement can flatten
Between the readerly and the writerly text
questions.explain: Egri's premise and McKee's controlling idea treat meaning as primary; Sontag warns against reducing a work to its meaning.

questions.q: Which is the most accurate summary of 'Against Interpretation'?
choices: Art has no meaning and shouldn't be analyzed
Critics should explain works by their authors' lives
Only popular art deserves attention
Interpretation that translates a work into a hidden meaning can stop us experiencing it
questions.explain: The 'art has no meaning' version is a myth; she objected to interpretation that replaces the work.

questions.q: How did Sontag's view of images of suffering change by Regarding the Pain of Others (2003)?
choices: She questioned her earlier claim that repeated exposure simply numbs viewers
She decided photographs should never show suffering
She argued photographs explain events better than words
She abandoned writing about photography altogether
questions.explain: She partly revised On Photography's argument, while insisting images need narrative and context.

questions.q: A photo editor has a powerful image of a famine victim. What does Sontag's later work suggest?
choices: Run it without a caption so it speaks for itself
Never run it
Run it with words that give context, cause and responsibility, or it risks becoming spectacle
Crop it until it looks like a painting
questions.explain: An image can command attention, but understanding comes from narrative and argument around it.

questions.q: A reviewer explains that the rumbling tank in a film is 'really' a phallic symbol. What is Sontag's complaint?
choices: The reviewer ignored the author's biography
The reviewer missed the film's inciting incident
The reviewer translated an image into a hidden meaning instead of attending to what it does
The reviewer was too sensuous in their response
questions.explain: 'X is really Y' is exactly the interpretive habit the essay attacks.

ideas: In place of a hermeneutics we need an erotics of art.
Interpreting a work as a code for a hidden meaning can be a way of taming it so it no longer has to be felt.
Images of suffering can haunt us, but understanding has to come from words, context and argument.
A critic's job is to show how a work is what it is, not to translate what it means.
